item.title: Indonesia’s magnitude 7.7 quake kills at least 51, displaces thousands
item.description:
Quake struck Flores region early on Saturday, prompting thousands to seek higher ground for fear of a tsunami A 7.7-magnitude earthquake that struck eastern Indonesia has killed at least 47 people, causing widespread panic and collapsing buildings and homes in a region prone to deadly seismic events. Rescuers have yet to reach Nagekeo, the area closest to the epicentre, because roads were blocked by landslides and communications disrupted. Continue reading...

item.title: West Bank: Palestinian families besieged for a week as settler violence continues
item.description:
As a general rule, I support Israel in its conflicts with adversaries like Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran. While I am no great fan of either the present Israeli government or the ideology of Zionism, Israel upholds liberal democratic values to a far greater extent than any of its enemies, and their victory would be a terrible catastrophe. Thus, I've even gone so far as to argue that it is a mistake for the Israelis to make hostage exchange deals with groups like Hamas, because doing so encourages more more terrorism. But it is also important to remember that not all Israeli actions are just, and that Palestinian Arabs also have human rights that must be respected. This is one of those times where these points must be emphasized. Over the last few years, Israeli settlers on the West Bank have repeatedly attacked Palestinians living there, seeking to force them off their land. These actions…

item.title: Israeli strikes kill 11 in southern Lebanon, Hezbollah threatens to retaliate
item.description:
Rescue services search for survivors and bodies after airstrikes hit homes in Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani Eleven people have been killed, including three children, and 19 injured in two Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon, the worst toll since deals in June brought a lull in hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah. Israeli warplanes bombed a home on the outskirts of the village of Ansar, killing seven people and flattening the building early on Saturday morning. Rescue services were working at the site to try to find survivors and locate bodies. Continue reading...

item.title: American missionary kidnapped in Niger freed after nine months
item.description:
An American missionary held in captivity in Niger for nine months will soon reunite with his family. Christian missionary pilot Kevin Rideout is free and safe with American officials after his kidnapping last year, his mission organization said Friday. It is not yet known how he escaped captivity or what group was holding him, but Islamist terror groups run rampant in Niger. Rideout, a father of four, was working with the Evangelical organization Serving in Mission (SIM) when he was kidnapped from Niamey, Niger, on October 21, 2025. “We are grateful to confirm that our good friend and brother in Christ, Kevin Rideout, has been released after over nine months in captivity,” the organization said in a statement. “Kevin is in good health in the care of US officials. He will soon be reunited with Krista [Rideout’s wife], his children, and his extended family.” President Donald Trump…

item.title: Massive egg recall in US south and south-west due to salmonella outbreak
item.description:
Eggs displayed in refrigerated section of a grocery store. —Lindsey Nicholson—Universal Images Group An egg recall linked to a salmonella outbreak was upgraded to the highest possible risk level by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Wednesday. item.title: Congo Ebola outbreak on track to become deadliest in history
item.description:
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo spread to a sixth province as the overall death toll surpassed 2,100 and cases topped 4,500. Experts say the virus may have been transmitted undetected for months, while health workers have struggled to contain the outbreak with poor medical supplies and no approved vaccine for the new strain — though several are in the works. The head of the World Health Organization this week warned that the current outbreak threatens to be the biggest ever, with authorities playing catch-up to the disease after “ a big head start. ” During the previous deadliest outbreak, which killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016, authorities had recorded 755 cases at the same point . — Jeronimo Gonzalez

Sources: PBS NewsHour, Semafor, The Guardian

item.title: Why France's under-15 social media ban was blocked
item.description:
France's attempt to ban social media for under-15s has been blocked by the Constitutional Council, which ruled the measure unconstitutional. Speaking to FRANCE 24, Peter Craddock, Senior Attorney advising social media companies, said the decision was unsurprising, arguing that the proposed law imposed a blanket ban without taking into account differences between platforms or children's levels of maturity. The court found that the measure infringed on the fundamental freedom of expression and information.

Covered by 2 public.
Sources: BBC News, France 24

item.title: Italy recovers millions of euros worth of stolen Renoir, Cézanne and Matisse paintings
item.description:
Italian authorities have recovered three paintings by Renoir, Cézanne and Matisse, worth more than €9 million, months after they were stolen from a private museum near Parma. Five Moldovan suspects have been detained, with police saying the gang had carefully planned the heist and was equipped to disable the museum's security systems.

item.title: Douglass breaks 50m freestyle swimming world record, Ledecky loses 800m
item.description:
American clocks 23.19sec to win final at Pan Pacs Douglass had first broken record with 23.49sec in heats Kate Douglass lowered her own world record in the women’s 50m freestyle for the second time in one day, winning the Pan Pacific Championships final in 23.19sec. In the morning preliminaries, the 24-year-old American swam 23.49 to take the mark away from teammate Gretchen Walsh, who finished second in the evening final in 23.74. Australia’s reigning world champion Meg Harris was third in 23.89. Continue reading...

item.title: Thousands displaced by deadly Indonesia earthquake as rescue efforts continue
item.description:
Searchers dig through collapsed buildings and debris after 7.7 magnitude quake killed at least 51 people Rescue crews dug through collapsed buildings and landslide debris in eastern Indonesia on Sunday as they searched for bodies and possible survivors a day after a powerful earthquake killed at least 51 people, injured more than 100 and displaced thousands. At least 24 people died in Manggarai regency and 17 in neighbouring East Manggarai, with additional fatalities reported in Sikka, Ngada and Ende regencies, the national disaster management agency said. Rescuers were still searching for people feared buried beneath landslides triggered by the quake across six regencies on Flores, a predominantly Catholic island in Muslim-majority Indonesia.
